rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and acknowledges image limitations, but it likely overstates confidence in clearly identifying an AA ICM/TE from this single somewhat soft-focus image.
Thoroughly integrates age, prior live birth, BMI, sperm quality, endometrium, oocyte yield, and diagnostic uncertainty with embryo quality and prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent overall; probability estimate is plausible, though slightly conservative for a 20-year-old with a reported 3AA embryo and prior live birth.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and aligned with standard IVF practice, especially single embryo transfer and avoiding low-evidence add-ons; minor overreach in some generalized counseling details.
Provides clear practical next steps for transfer management, luteal support adherence, SET recommendation, lifestyle counseling, and structured contingency planning if implantation fails.
